_how: Recipe for shorts.build (video-machine). 9 clips from Part 2 of 2 of the NOWRA booth series with Jason Birdsong of JT Services (take c0031, Sony 1920x1080 at 29.97 fps, one static wide shot: Jason left, Ashley right; two wireless mics, LEFT channel Ashley, RIGHT channel Jason). keep = inclusive word-index ranges of 02_audio/words/c0031.json in play order; the host's 1 to 4 word back-channel interjections are split out; stammers stay in the audio and are hidden from the captions with "" fixes; fillers skip automatically; max_gap 1.0. layout crop at 0.23 (Jason), crop_at cuts to Ashley (0.74) for her lines in break-even-job and bonus-bob. end_channel right keeps only Jason's mic from the last word on. mono: true mixes the two mics into both ears. Posting plan: Part 2 releases Wednesday 2026-11-11 (8:00 CT). Part 1's Shorts (2026-10-26-podcast-nowra-birdsong) hold 3 PM CT Wed to Sun and 3 and 5 PM Mon/Tue 11-09/10, so these take noon every day Wed 11-11 to Tue 11-17 plus 5 PM Mon 11-16 and Tue 11-17: two Shorts a day across both parts. Every clip goes to YouTube and TikTok; the five strongest (break-even-job, price-never-problem, cover-payroll, pay-more-taxes, disposal-crisis) also to Instagram and Facebook, one a weekday at noon (Wed to Fri overlap Part 1's 3 PM Instagram posts: move one part's if Ashley wants one Instagram post a day). Captions: one per network; {jt} tags JT Services (jtserviceco.com lists no social accounts, so it is a plain name), the full episode linked ({episode}) everywhere but Facebook. NAWT = National Association of Wastewater Technicians (Jason is its president). approved = Ashley approved it in Ops. Generated by 07_notes/make_shorts.py.

clips.title:
Do you know your break-even
on a *septic* job?

youtube.title: Are you losing money on septic jobs? Know your break-even number

captions.instagram:
Breaking even isn't losing.

Jason Birdsong of {jt} says if you leave an aerobic unit call with a $99 diagnostic, you lost money once you count the fuel, the time and the call center. Do it at your $500 break-even and you still paid the bills and kept your tech's family fed. Agree?

Full episode: {episode}

#septic #septicbusiness #knowyournumbers #breakeven #septicowner
captions.facebook:
Here's a question Jason Birdsong of JT Services asked me: your break-even to change an air pump on an aerobic unit is $500. Are you winning or losing if you do the job for $500? I said losing. He said most people would. But if your tech drives out, burns the fuel and the time, the call center books it, and you leave with a $99 diagnostic, you lost. At $500 you still paid the bills and kept Johnny and his family fed. You don't want to do that every time, but it's not losing. Do you know your break-even on a job?

#septic #smallbusiness

youtube.title: Price is never the problem for a septic company. Value is.

captions.instagram:
Price is never the problem.

Jason Birdsong of {jt} says yes, you should go up on your prices. But if you can't back it with the value, you're not going to sell anything. So many people have sales trauma and blame the price. And if you don't know your numbers, how do you sell the value? Agree?

Full episode: {episode}

#septic #septicbusiness #pricing #sales #septicowner
captions.facebook:
Everybody in this industry tells everybody to raise their prices. Jason Birdsong of JT Services agrees, but he wants to know why. Is it 10%? 5%? What's the strategy? His point is that if you can't back a price with the value, you're not going to sell anything. So many people have what he calls sales trauma: they can't sell it, so they decide the price is too high. He says price is never the problem. And if you don't know your own numbers, how do you sell the value? Have you raised your prices this year?

#septic #smallbusiness

clips.title:
We had to move money
to cover *payroll*

youtube.title: The septic owner's wake-up call: we had to move money to cover payroll

captions.instagram:
I thought we were way past this.

Jason Birdsong of {jt} and his wife learned their numbers, hired some leadership and got complacent. Then she called: we're going to have to move some money around to cover payroll. Her answer for how it happened was simple. We've been lazy.

Full episode: {episode}

#septic #septicbusiness #knowyournumbers #payroll #septicowner
captions.facebook:
Jason Birdsong of JT Services told me about a phone call from his wife. They had learned their numbers, hired some leadership, and stopped looking at those numbers every day. Then she called and said they were going to have to move some money around to cover payroll. He said he thought they were way past this. She said, we've been lazy. He called it his self-reflection moment, and they had to get right back into knowing their numbers and dig their way back out. Has that ever happened to you?

#septic #smallbusiness

clips.title:
Why I want my septic
business to pay *more* taxes

youtube.title: Why this septic business owner wants to pay more taxes

captions.instagram:
If you're paying taxes, you're profitable.

Jason Birdsong of {jt} says that's the mind shift that has to happen as you grow. He wants to pay more taxes. As you scale, you need money, and if your balance sheet shows no profit because you're dodging taxes, it's hard to borrow. Agree?

Full episode: {episode}

#septic #septicbusiness #taxes #smallbusiness #septicowner
captions.facebook:
Most business owners I know work hard to pay as little in taxes as they can. Jason Birdsong of JT Services says that has to change as you grow into a three, five or six million dollar company. His mindset now is that if you're paying taxes, you're profitable, so he wants to pay more. Here's the part people miss: as you scale, you need money. If your balance sheet shows you're not making any because you didn't want to pay taxes, it's hard to borrow. Do you see it that way?

#septic #smallbusiness

clips.title:
Florida lost half its
*septage* disposal sites

youtube.title: The septage disposal crisis: Florida went from 42 sites to 24

captions.instagram:
Florida went from 42 septage disposal sites to 24 in less than a year.

Jason Birdsong of {jt}, president of NAWT, says several states are in crisis over where to take septage. The government fix will take time, so NAWT is teaching pumpers to treat their own septage or dispose of it properly. Is it getting harder where you are?

Full episode: {episode}

#septic #septicpumping #septage #septicbusiness #pumper
captions.facebook:
If you pump septic tanks, this one matters. Jason Birdsong of JT Services is the president of NAWT, and he told me several states are in a real crisis over where to take septage. At the NOWRA conference he heard that Florida went from 42 statewide disposal sites to 24, cut in half in less than a year. He believes it's going to take some time for the government to fix it, so NAWT is building programs to teach pumpers how to treat their own septage or at least dispose of it properly. Is disposal getting harder where you are?

#septic #septicpumping
